clue.text: The point of the quarrel, maybe?

definitions.text: The point of the quarrel, maybe?

parts.words: The point of the quarrel, maybe?
parts.note: a quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, so its point is the sharp tip at the front of that missile, not the heart of an argument

explanation.surface: Someone asks what an argument was really about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' reads as a row, but it is the old word for a short, square-headed crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip fixed to the front of a bolt or shaft is its head.

clue.text: Revolutionary way to grow crops

parts.note: a revolutionary method turns round in a cycle, and farmers change crops field by field in a repeating sequence

explanation.surface: An agricultural innovation is hailed as radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical new idea; here it means going round, as farmers cycle crops through their fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers vary crops in a fixed cycle, turning each field through a sequence of plantings.

clue.text: The earth's five main features

parts.note: the main here is the sea, so the planet's five main features are its great bodies of salt water

explanation.surface: A geography lesson lists the planet's chief characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is an old word for the open sea, so the five 'main features' are the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, Arctic and Southern.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographers count five great seas covering most of the planet's surface.

clue.text: The blooming best part of life!

definitions.text: The blooming best part of life!

parts.words: The blooming best part of life!
parts.note: blooming means flourishing, so this is the period of life when someone is at the peak of their powers

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some stage of life is the bloody best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British swear word for emphasis, but it describes the flowering, prime-of-life period.
explanation.definitionFit: One's prime is the time of greatest vigour and success.

clue.text: Literally the result of cutting down work?

definitions.text: Literally the result of cutting down work?

parts.words: Literally the result of cutting down work?
parts.note: a shortened edition of a book is the result of cutting down a work; read literally the phrase also describes a version with a bridge in it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what follows a reduction in workload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' invites splitting the first word as A BRIDGED: a version with a bridge, while a shortened text is the plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened edition of a text is one that has been condensed or cut.

clue.text: Strangely clear it is and life-like

indicators.note: doing something strangely means in an odd order, so these clue letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an odd picture is clear and true to nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges the letters of CLEAR IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true to nature resembles real life closely.

clue.text: Two chessmen netting small river fish

parts.note: a king is one chess piece

indicators.note: netting means catching in a net, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a pawn is another chess piece
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Two chess pieces catch fish in a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two chessmen' supplies two separate pieces, and 'netting' has the second catch the river abbreviation; 'fish' is loose, as the answer is a crustacean.
explanation.definitionFit: A large prawn is a shellfish, called fish loosely in fishmongers' and crossword usage.

clue.text: Shocking swimmers?

parts.note: shocking seems to mean scandalous, but these sea creatures deliver a painful wound from a barbed tail

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled by a group of bathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' reads as outrageous; here it describes sea creatures that hurt with a barbed tail.
explanation.definitionFit: These flat sea fish carry a venomous spine and give a painful wound.

clue.text: Is among those left to carry on the fight

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the rest are those remaining

explanation.surface: A soldier is one of the survivors who keep fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' signals the container; 'those left' means the remainder, a noun, not the left wing in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose and fight back is to keep struggling against something.

clue.text: A 3-ft metal balance?

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy
a yard is three feet long

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a weighing scale made of metal, three feet long.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the split reading: a yard of steel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a weighing scale with a sliding weight on an uneven arm.

clue.text: Make a big hit with an advertising catch-phrase

parts.note: to slog is to hit a ball hard, as in cricket
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advertiser hopes a catchy line will be a big success.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOG, a hard swiping hit in cricket, is followed by AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A short memorable phrase used in marketing is the standard sense.

clue.text: Flags sticklers for propriety don't want to see lowered

definitions.text: sticklers for propriety don't want to see lowered
definitions.meaning: people strict about correct behaviour hate to see moral levels drop

explanation.surface: Traditionalists dislike seeing flags lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'lowered' standards: banners are lowered, and so are moral levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Banners are standards, and so are the levels of conduct that sticklers insist on.

clue.text: Enormous interest is taken in his activities

definitions.text: Enormous interest is taken in his activities

parts.words: Enormous interest is taken in his activities
parts.note: interest seems to mean attention, but it is the charge on a loan, taken in excessive amounts by an extortionate lender

explanation.surface: A man's doings attract huge public attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' reads as curiosity; here it is money charged on a loan, which this lender takes at punishing rates.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive rates on loans makes enormous interest his trade.

clue.text: One who is too pernickety to make an inventory

definitions.meaning: someone excessively attached to rules and correct forms
read as three words, to draw up an itemised record

explanation.surface: A fussy person is asked to draw up a list.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FORM A LIST, the answer means to make an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler for strict rules and forms is overly fussy, and drawing up a record means compiling items.

clue.text: Those who can will appreciate the value of notes

definitions.text: Those who can will appreciate the value of notes

parts.words: Those who can will appreciate the value of notes
parts.note: notes look like banknotes, but here they are musical notes, whose time values a trained musician understands from the score

explanation.surface: People who are able know what money is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Value of notes' sounds like money; in music a note's value is its length, which anyone who can interpret a score grasps.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to interpret a score means understanding written musical symbols.

clue.text: A step for the visitor to 25?

definitions.text: A step for the visitor to 25?

parts.words: A step for the visitor to 25?
parts.note: the visitor must step over a doorstep, and clue 25's answer means to go to the other side, so this is what is stepped across at the entrance

explanation.surface: Someone asks what stage a guest goes through.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference to 25 across, meaning go to the other side, points to the doorstep that a visitor steps across.
explanation.definitionFit: The doorstep at an entrance is the strip a visitor steps over.

clue.text: Determined to stop running?

definitions.meaning: jelly, glue or concrete stop flowing when they harden

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved to give up jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests jogging; the second sense is of a liquid that firms up and no longer flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolved means fixed in purpose, and a liquid that firms up has hardened.

clue.text: Is upset about a capuchin monkey

indicators.note: about means going around, so the turned piece surrounds the other
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is troubled about a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns IS to SI, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: The sai is a South American capuchin monkey, a crossword regular.

clue.text: Attempt to hear the case

definitions.meaning: a judge hears a case in court

explanation.surface: A judge sets out to listen to a legal dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs: to make an effort, and to judge a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is a go, and a court that hears a case puts the accused on trial.

clue.text: A superior system of training

parts.note: superior here means placed above, and a system of training is a network for running trains, so an elevated rail line

explanation.surface: A school claims an excellent teaching method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' means higher up, not better, and 'training' is read as the running of trains: an elevated railway such as Liverpool's former one.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated rail line runs on structures raised above the street.

clue.text: Climber found to be in league with eight US colleges

definitions.meaning: a creeping plant that grows up walls

definitions.text: in league with eight US colleges
definitions.meaning: the elite group of eight north-eastern US universities bears this plant's name

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is in league with American colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a person; it is a plant. The Ivy League is the group of eight old universities such as Harvard and Yale.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen creeper gives its name to the elite American university league.

clue.text: Comparatively crazy red dyestuff

definitions.meaning: a plant whose root yields a red dye

explanation.surface: An even crazier red colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: More insane is the comparative of mad, and the plant root gives a traditional red dye.

clue.text: Remarks that are made incidentally

parts.note: passing comments, especially those an actor speaks to the audience while other characters do not hear

explanation.surface: A description of throwaway comments.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain description, with a nod to the stage, where actors make such remarks to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing comments made in parenthesis, off the main subject, are by-the-way remarks.

clue.text: Fragmented design of a great lawgiver

definitions.meaning: a picture made of small pieces of tile or glass
relating to Moses, who gave the Ten Commandments

explanation.surface: A broken pattern belonging to a famous lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective for Moses, the biblical lawgiver, matches a design built of small tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiled picture is assembled from fragments, and the law of Moses is so called.

clue.text: Outburst of anger about a leader of great power

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
an outburst scatters things, so these letters burst apart into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry outburst concerns a powerful leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outburst of' rearranges ANGER into REGAN, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was US president, head of a superpower.

clue.text: One vote too many to go to the other side

definitions.text: to go to the other side

parts.note: a voter marks a ballot paper with a cross
over means in excess, as in over budget

explanation.surface: A single extra vote makes someone defect to the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: A vote on a ballot paper is a cross; 'too many' is OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Going across to the far side, or changing party, is a crossing of sides.

clue.text: Is soundly appreciative of the joke?

definitions.text: Is soundly appreciative of the joke?

parts.words: Is soundly appreciative of the joke?
parts.note: soundly means thoroughly but also with noise, so this is showing amusement audibly

explanation.surface: Someone fully enjoys a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'; it means making a sound, as an amused listener does.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing amusement out loud is chuckling or chortling.

clue.text: The air force register?

parts.note: an air force looks like the RAF, but read as the force of the air it is the strength of wind, and a register is an instrument that records it

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the RAF's list of personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air force' reads as a military service; it is the force of moving air, and 'register' is a measuring instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemometer is an instrument recording the speed of moving air.

clue.text: Tumbles that may be made light of

definitions.text: that may be made light of
definitions.meaning: thin strips of wood or paper used to carry a flame, so light is made from them

explanation.surface: Falls that someone shrugs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made light of' suggests shrugging off; the second sense is tapers, things a light is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Falls are tumbles, and tapers of wood or paper are used for lighting fires.

clue.text: Instantly canonised by special arrangement

indicators.note: letters set out by a special arrangement are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is made a saint without delay through a special deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By special arrangement' rearranges the letters of CANONISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Very quickly, in a moment's time, means immediately.
